name: The Scraps, 19 January 1998, Part 1

date.source: The post's banner reads January 19, 1997, an evident slip for 1998: the show follows Rasslefest of 4 January 1998, which its opening interview recalls.

notes: The first of four parts of the Scraps of 19 January 1998.

evidence.note: The first of four parts of the Scraps of 19 January 1998.

matches.note: Bobby McAllister, with Victoria Glenn, countered Nik Nyce's Standing Nycely set-up into a DDT and pinned him in both men's debut.

name: The Scraps, 19 January 1998, Part 2

date.source: The post carries no banner: it is the second of four parts of the Scraps posted on 19 January 1998, whose first part is dated there.

notes: The second of four parts of the Scraps of 19 January 1998: the Siberian Express against the Pros, the TV title match of Rock Bottom Robbie and Doug Adams, and the German Eagles against Phi Theta Kappa; between the matches Ken Curtis crashes the broadcast to protest the World title contender.

evidence.note: The second of four parts of the Scraps of 19 January 1998: the Siberian Express against the Pros, the TV title match of Rock Bottom Robbie and Doug Adams, and the German Eagles against Phi Theta Kappa; between the matches Ken Curtis crashes the broadcast to protest the World title contender.

matches.note: The Siberian Express ambushed the Pros at the bell and used the referee's blind side for illegal tags; Grant pinned Andrei Bolotov after the Pros hit Pro-Pain.
TV champion Rock Bottom Robbie beat Doug "Grizzly" Adams, who came out without Nemesis, with the Rock Bottom Slam.
Joseph Eagle pinned Brad Thompson after the Eagles' Double German Suplex, the Eagles beating Phi Theta Kappa.

name: The Scraps, 19 January 1998, Part 3

date.source: The post carries no banner: it is the third of four parts of the Scraps posted on 19 January 1998, whose first part is dated there.

notes: The third of four parts of the Scraps of 19 January 1998: Prodigy attacks Aladdin Style on the ramp before their match, and J.W. Hardin and Derek Mota's match ends in a referee's wrong call, a stretcher and a no contest ruled by the president.

evidence.note: The third of four parts of the Scraps of 19 January 1998: Prodigy attacks Aladdin Style on the ramp before their match, and J.W. Hardin and Derek Mota's match ends in a referee's wrong call, a stretcher and a no contest ruled by the president.

matches.note: Prodigy, with Black Kat, jumped Style on the ramp before the bell and won with a re-reversal of Style's small package after Wellington had waved off an earlier three-count.

Hardin's figure four ended with Hans Foresmits ringing the bell for a submission; Mota then threw a stretcher at Hardin and pinned him, Ed Jaspard announced a Mota pinfall on Tommy Gregory's word, and President Grey came out and ruled it a no contest.

name: The Scraps, 19 January 1998, Part 4

date.source: The post carries no banner: it is the last of four parts of the Scraps posted on 19 January 1998, whose first part is dated there; its commentary recalls Rasslefest of 4 January 1998.

notes: The last of four parts of the Scraps of 19 January 1998: Ken Curtis beats Stanlee Maxx, and the SCRA World title match of Eddy Jacks and Gangsta Impasse ends in a disqualification after a run of interference, closed by Curtis dressed as a concession worker.

evidence.note: The last of four parts of the Scraps of 19 January 1998: Ken Curtis beats Stanlee Maxx, and the SCRA World title match of Eddy Jacks and Gangsta Impasse ends in a disqualification after a run of interference, closed by Curtis dressed as a concession worker.

matches.note: Curtis attacked Maxx from behind as he checked the ropes and beat the 350-pound Maxx with High Noon.

For the SCRA World title: Gangsta Impasse, with John Drake, fought Jacks, who came out behind the Praetorian Guard beside Savarese; after the Guard double-suplexed Impasse on the floor and Drake hit the Guard with a chair, Ken Curtis, dressed as a concession worker, hit Impasse with a hot-dog warmer and Ed Jaspard announced Impasse the winner by disqualification.

notes: The first of four parts of the Scraps of 26 January 1998: the card, a recorded reply from Aladdin Style, Phantom's unannounced opener against Latexman Art Vandilay while newcomer Chase Hunter heckles the commentators, and a three-way of Nik Nyce, Bobby McAllister and Anthony Logan.

evidence.note: The first of four parts of the Scraps of 26 January 1998: the card, a recorded reply from Aladdin Style, Phantom's unannounced opener against Latexman Art Vandilay while newcomer Chase Hunter heckles the commentators, and a three-way of Nik Nyce, Bobby McAllister and Anthony Logan.

matches.note: Phantom attacked the Latexman from behind, was distracted by Chase Hunter's act and won by reversing the Latexman's roll-up.
Logan and Nyce teamed to pin McAllister first, then fought each other; Logan won with the Dragonstrike Heart Punch.

name: The Scraps, 9 February 1998, Part 1

date.source: The post's banner reads LIVE FEBRUARY 9, 1997, the same year slip as the January and February pages; read as 1998 because the post is dated 9 February 1998 (a Monday, the 'Monday Night Scraps' of its opening line), is set in the park of 'the Winter Carnival the night before' and looks ahead to Spring Spectacle on 15 March.

notes: The first of five parts of the Scraps of 9 February 1998: the card (the steel cage for a World title shot, the Activists against the German Eagles, the tag triple threat and the first round of the North American tournament), then Derek Mota beats Rock Bottom Robbie with Aladdin Style's help.

evidence.note: The first of five parts of the Scraps of 9 February 1998: the card (the steel cage for a World title shot, the Activists against the German Eagles, the tag triple threat and the first round of the North American tournament), then Derek Mota beats Rock Bottom Robbie with Aladdin Style's help.

matches.note: North American Tournament Match 1: Mota attacks Robbie as he stands on the top rope and the referee, Wellington, has to call for the bell; Robbie spinebusters and powerbombs him, then Style comes out, hits Robbie from the apron (Jack Hazard: 'a pair of brass knucks') and Mota pins him with the Death Flip.

name: The Scraps, 9 February 1998, Part 2

date.source: The post carries no banner: it is the second of five parts posted on 9 February 1998, whose first part is dated there.

notes: The second of five parts of the Scraps of 9 February 1998: Sean Watts beats Mike Justice with the Seatleplex, and Bobby McAllister beats Gwaii Edenshaw by countout while Nik Nyce and Justice brawl at ringside.

evidence.note: The second of five parts of the Scraps of 9 February 1998: Sean Watts beats Mike Justice with the Seatleplex, and Bobby McAllister beats Gwaii Edenshaw by countout while Nik Nyce and Justice brawl at ringside.

matches.note: North American Tournament Match 2: Watts attacks Justice at the bell and is hauled off by the referee; Justice works Watts's leg with the figure four and Texas Cloverleaf, Watts's knee gives out on his first Seatleplex and he lands a second for the three.

North American Tournament Match 3: Nik Nyce and Mike Justice come to ringside and brawl, Tommy Gregory holds McAllister back, and Edenshaw, thrown over the railing, is a few inches from the mat when the referee reaches ten and calls the bell.

name: The Scraps, 9 February 1998, Part 3

date.source: The post carries no banner: it is the third of five parts posted on 9 February 1998, whose first part is dated there.

notes: The third of five parts of the Scraps of 9 February 1998: Aladdin Style beats Sgt. Pepper with the Texas Cloverleaf, Prodigy trains with Black Kat and talks about the cage match, and Andrei Bolotov wins the tag team triple threat over Walt Jabasco and Bill Baer with the bear hug.

evidence.note: The third of five parts of the Scraps of 9 February 1998: Aladdin Style beats Sgt. Pepper with the Texas Cloverleaf, Prodigy trains with Black Kat and talks about the cage match, and Andrei Bolotov wins the tag team triple threat over Walt Jabasco and Bill Baer with the bear hug.

matches.note: North American Tournament Match 4: Style's knee gives out on a moonsault, but he takes Pepper apart with a rolling kick and an Indian deathlock; Pepper rallies with a belly to belly and a clothesline and gets a two count, and Style ends it with the Texas Cloverleaf.

matches.stipulation: Tag Team Triple Threat Match, elimination style, by pinfall or submission; the winning team gets a pay per view title shot
matches.note: Tommy Gregory pushes the managers and partners back from the ring so that the match is clean. Bolotov makes Baer submit to the bear hug, then locks it on Jabasco twice, the second time for the submission, and the Siberian Express earn the tag title shot at Spring Spectacle.

eliminations.note: submitted to the bear hug

matches.note: For the SCRA tag team titles: Ocki the Moselman lies on the mat and makes the referee stop the Activists' count and miss a tag; Comrades Inc. then walk down, Comrade Jonah Ulanov distracts the referee, Comrade Johnstone hits Chris Eagle with a Russian flag and Comrade Zangief spins him into a piledriver. Zak Rage drapes an arm over Chris Eagle for the three and the Activists are the new champions, which Jon Grey says is not how they would have wanted to win.

matches.stipulation: Steel Cage World Title Shot Match; no countouts or disqualifications, out of the cage only by pinfall or submission
matches.note: Gangsta Impasse wins the last fall. Pinfalls send the men out one at a time: Prodigy is pinned by Impasse as Hardin also covers him, Hunter drops from the top of the cage, hits Nik Nyce in the head with a Chia Pet and pins him, Impasse pins Hunter with the Gangsta Impact, and in the last pair Street Smarts climbs the cage and drops a snow pile on Hardin so that Impasse can pin him with the Helleplex. Jon Grey says Impasse faces Ken Curtis at Spring Spectacle, and Impasse runs up the ramp to fight Curtis at once.

eliminations.note: pinned by Impasse as Hardin also covers him; Jon Grey says he is the first man to have to leave

name: The Scraps, 16 February 1998, Part 1

date.source: The post's banner reads LIVE FEBRUARY 16, 1997, the same year slip as the January and February pages; read as 1998 because the post is dated 16 February 1998, a Monday (16 February 1997 was a Sunday), and the card carries on from the Scraps of 9 February: the North American tournament continues with Derek Mota against Sean Watts, Ken Curtis's barn is in ashes and he opens a series of World title defences with Prodigy.

notes: The first of six parts of the Scraps of 16 February 1998: a taped Ken Curtis promo in the ashes of his barn aimed at Gangsta Impasse, Jon Grey's interview with Chase Hunter, who arrives in a leopard-fur loincloth until Gwaii Edenshaw attacks him, the night's card, Rock Bottom Robbie's win over "Hot Stuff" Mike Justice after Hunter burns Justice's hands with a hot coal, and Keith Spencer's interview with Nik Nyce, which ends in a brawl with Bobby McAllister.

evidence.note: The first of six parts of the Scraps of 16 February 1998: a taped Ken Curtis promo in the ashes of his barn aimed at Gangsta Impasse, Jon Grey's interview with Chase Hunter, who arrives in a leopard-fur loincloth until Gwaii Edenshaw attacks him, the night's card, Rock Bottom Robbie's win over "Hot Stuff" Mike Justice after Hunter burns Justice's hands with a hot coal, and Keith Spencer's interview with Nik Nyce, which ends in a brawl with Bobby McAllister.

matches.note: One fall, 20-minute limit: Justice attacks as Robbie climbs into the ring, and Robbie fights back and follows him outside; Chase Hunter walks down with a jar, speaks to Robbie and drops hot coal on Justice's hand (Jon Grey: 'It's a hot coal! Justice's hands are burning!'), and Robbie pulls Justice back into the ring and pins him with the Rock Bottom Slam.

notes: The second of six parts of the Scraps of 16 February 1998: Ted Jaspard's return beside his brother Ed, the Pros against Comrades Inc., Keith Spencer's interview with Alexander Gudonov and the Siberian Express about their tag title shot at Spring Spectacle, and Nik Nyce against Gwaii Edenshaw with interference from Sir John Caboto, Chase Hunter and Bobby McAllister.

matches.note: Grant starts against Johnstone, and Jack Hazard walks out of the arena calling it the most boring match in history; Jon Grey commentates alone for a while and Hazard returns. As the Pros set up the Pro Pain, Johnstone breaks out of it, clotheslines Jabasco over the top and slams Grant for the three; Jon Grey: 'Comrades Inc. win!'

One fall, 40-minute limit: Edenshaw attacks Nyce before the bell and Sir John Caboto helps with his cane and by shaking the ropes. Nyce answers Caboto's raised cane with a mule kick and takes over; Chase Hunter drops from a bungee cord and leaves a puzzle piece at Nyce's feet, and while the referee turns to Hunter, Bobby McAllister hits Nyce with a chair and Edenshaw rolls him up. Nyce reverses the roll-up for the three (Jon Grey: 'Nyce gets the pin!').

notes: The third of six parts of the Scraps of 16 February 1998: the four-way dance of Bobby McAllister, Aladdin Style, Chase Hunter and "Golden" Ponyboy Kertins, which Style wins by rolling up Kertins while Hunter and Edenshaw, and McAllister and Nik Nyce, brawl at ringside.

matches.stipulation: Four-Way Dance; one fall, 30-minute time limit, the men tagging in and out
matches.note: Four-way dance, one fall, 30-minute limit, the men tagging in and out. Kertins comes down with the Greasers and Cherry and Wellington has them all leave the ring; McAllister and Style work toward their match of the next week, Style tags in Hunter, and Kertins nearly scores with an abdominal stretch and a camel clutch. Edenshaw walks in to brawl with Hunter and Nyce to brawl with McAllister, and while Kertins looks to the outside Style grabs him from behind in a roll-up for the three.

matches.note: Comrade Jonah Ulanov takes Jack Hazard's seat for money. Dragovich and the Eagles trade near-falls; Alexander Gudonov gets up on the apron to distract the referee, Comrade Zangief drives the Russian flag into Chris Eagle's head and powerslams him, and Bolotov holds Joseph Eagle in a bear hug while Dragovich hits a running clothesline (Jon Grey: 'IRON CURTAIN, and it is over') for the three. After the match Zangief and Johnstone attack the Eagles with a Russian Spinning Piledriver and a Ukrainian Bear Clutch, Ulanov leaves the desk and gets Johnstone to break the hold, and Sengir runs out to clear the ring; Joseph Eagle is wheeled out by paramedics.

notes: The fifth of six parts of the Scraps of 16 February 1998: Derek Mota against "The Iconoclast" Sean Watts, which ends with Aladdin Style hitting Watts with Sengir's belt and Mota's pin, Sengir and Jezra Wagner staging a pin and an announcement over the unconscious Watts, and the start of "Outlaw" J.W. Hardin against Gangsta Impasse, which ends in part six.

evidence.note: The fifth of six parts of the Scraps of 16 February 1998: Derek Mota against "The Iconoclast" Sean Watts, which ends with Aladdin Style hitting Watts with Sengir's belt and Mota's pin, Sengir and Jezra Wagner staging a pin and an announcement over the unconscious Watts, and the start of "Outlaw" J.W. Hardin against Gangsta Impasse, which ends in part six.

matches.note: North American Tournament match: Watts nearly wins with a DDT, Mota tries an ankle lock, and Watts takes over and raises his hands to the crowd, then lifts his leg off Mota at two. Mota drops him with a backdrop and Watts stumbles out of the ring, where Aladdin Style hits him in the mouth with a title belt and Tommy Gregory chases Style with a chair; Mota lays a foot on the unconscious Watts for the three (Jon Grey: 'Guess somebody delivered this match to Mota...but why?'). Sengir then picks up the belt (Jon Grey: 'It's Sengir's belt!'), and he and Jezra Wagner, who has a referee's shirt under a trenchcoat, stage a pin on Watts, Jezra announces Sengir as the winner and the still ESWP World Junior Heavyweight Champion, and Sengir tells Watts they are even.

Hardin against Gangsta Impasse, which Ken Curtis, in a Dodgers cap, ends by bulldogging Impasse while Hardin distracts the referee, and Ken Curtis against Prodigy for the World title after President Grey strips Prodigy of the TV title, which ends when Street Smarts's interference gets Curtis disqualified.

matches.note: Begun in part five. Ken Curtis's voice booms over the speakers: he shows Impasse's Benz at the edge of Lake Ontario and shoves it into the water while Impasse watches from the ramp and Wellington does not count him out. A man in a Los Angeles Dodgers cap hops the rail behind Impasse while Hardin distracts the referee, bulldogs Impasse on the ramp and throws the cap onto him: it is Curtis ('It's called video, Grey!'). Curtis points a finger at Hardin as he backs up the ramp, and Wellington disqualifies Hardin. Jon Grey: 'a disqualification resulting in a win by Gangsta Impasse'.

matches.stipulation: World Title Match; one fall, 20-minute time limit
matches.note: President Grey strips Prodigy of the TV title for not defending it for two weeks and says he will give the status of the vacant belt next week. World title match, one fall, 20-minute limit: Prodigy works Curtis with technical holds, Curtis reverses a tombstone attempt into a spike, and after a dropkick sends Prodigy through the ropes Street Smarts walks in and bodyslams him (Jon Grey: 'The Ghetto Blaster!'). Jon Grey thinks the referee disqualified Ken Curtis, Jack Hazard says Street Smarts cost Curtis the match and that Curtis is no longer undefeated, and Jon Grey says Street Smarts also cost Prodigy the title. Prodigy goes after Gangsta Impasse, Street Smarts steps in and takes Last Ride In, and Impasse attacks Curtis.
